Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Subhash Chand
------
For the Petitioners : Mr. Sidhartha Roy, Advocate

For the State : Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, A.P.P.
 --------

The present criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed for quashing of order dated 5th February, 2015 passed by the learned Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi, whereby and whereunder the non- bailable warrant has been issued against the petitioners in connection with Complaint Case No.795 of 2013 registered under Sections 406,
420/34 of the I.P.C.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that on behalf of the petitioners, the order-sheet of Complaint Case No.795 of 2013 has been filed which is annexed as Annexure-1 to the present criminal miscellaneous petition.

On perusal of the order-sheet it appears that vide order dated 5th February, 2015, the learned trial court has issued non-bailable warrant against the accused persons and there was no report in regard to execution of the bailable warrant against the petitioners and subsequently on third date i.e., 5th February, 2015 the non-bailable warrant was issued without applying judicial mind.

In view of the record, it is apparent that the learned trial court without any report of execution of the bailable warrant, straight away on 5th February, 2015 issued the non-bailable warrant against the petitioners.

The same is against the settled propositions of law passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court,
wherein it has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that at first instance the summon should be issued and thereafter the bailable warrant and if despite execution of the same, the accused does not Raj Kishore Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand .... ....

entities.text: Inder Mohan Goswami and Anr vs State of Uttaranchal and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
reported in AIR 2008 SC 208 at paragraphs 52 and 53 has held as under :
"52.Non-bailable warrant should be issued to bring a person to court when summons of bailable warrants would be unlikely to have the desired result. This could be when :
* it is reasonable to believe that the person will not voluntarily appear in court; or *
the police authorities are unable to find the person to serve him with a summon; or *
it is considered that the person could harm someone if not placed into custody immediately.
53.As far as possible, if the court is of the opinion that a summon will suffice in getting the appearance of the accused in the court, the summon or the bailable warrants should be preferred.

The warrants either bailable or non-bailable should never be issued without proper scrutiny of facts and complete application of mind,
due to the extremely serious consequences and ramifications which ensue on issuance of warrants.
The court must very carefully examine whether the Criminal Complaint or SCW6692 FIR has not been filed with an oblique motive."

In view of the submissions made and materials available on record as well as keeping in view the aforesaid judicial pronouncement, this criminal miscellaneous petition is disposed of and the impugned order dated 5th February, 2015 is set aside, if the further proceeding has not commenced in the Complaint Case No.795 of 2013.
It is made clear that if the trial court had proceeded with the trial, this order will have no effect.
(Subhash Chand, J.) Rohit Raj Kishore Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... Opp. ... on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54950825/
